documents.content: An invented relay assigns x_0=5. Its proposed rule is x_(n+1)=x_n+3 for every nonnegative integer n. The only measured values supplied are x_0=5, x_1=8, x_2=11. State whether the universal rule is proved or only consistent with these observations; give its conditional prediction for x_3.

The same invented relay is now measured at x_3=15 and x_4=19, with previous observations x_0=5, x_1=8, x_2=11 confirmed unchanged. Measurements are exact for this synthetic problem. The universal increment-3 proposition predicts x_3=14. Determine the contradiction and preserve only the earlier statements that remain valid. No mechanism or later values are supplied.

A mechanism note for the same invented relay proposes x_(n+1)=x_n+3+I(n>=2), where I is 1 when its condition is true and 0 otherwise, with x_0=5. The note is a hypothesis, not proof of a physical mechanism. Check whether it fits all supplied observations x_0 through x_4. Derive a closed form for all nonnegative integer n conditional on the note, predict x_5, and distinguish fit, conditional derivation, and empirical confirmation. Assess the false twin x_n=5+4n for all n>=0.
